newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares continue recovery in bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares continue recovery in bourse trade.

text.p: The German share market continued its process of recovery on Wednesday after falling ten percent last week, and advanced to within around 100 points of its former all-time high in bourse trade.

The 30-share DAX index stood at 3,367.37 points, up 37.61 points or 1.13 percent, boosted chiefly by the strength of the dollar at 1.71 marks. Trade was also underpinned by a stronger overnight close on Wall Street.
"The dollar is the major theme today but the fact that New York seems to have stabilised is also helping," a Frankfurt trader said, although the market fell back slightly as bourse trade progressed.
Dealers said comments by U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs strategist Abby Joseph Cohen were also supportive after she said on Tuesday the market correction in the U.S. was over.
"Abby Joseph Cohen seems to be calling the shots at the moment, and if she says the market consolidation may be over, then we listen," a Frankfurt trader said.

One of the winners in early bourse was Fresenius Medical Care (FMC), the dialysis subsidiary of German medical group Fresenius AG. Shares rose on an upbeat reaction to an analysts' meeting on Tuesday and were up 7.60 marks, or 5.08 percent, at 157.30 marks an hour into bourse trade.
Exporters were lifted by the higher dollar. Luxury carmaker BMW AG was up 55 marks, or 4.10 percent, at 396 marks.
Chemicals were also higher, but fell victim to profit-taking later on, with the exception of Hoechst AG, which was up 1.48 marks, or or 2.2 percent, at 68.60 marks.
Bayer AG was up 0.62 percent at 69.75 marks off a high of 70.29 marks, while BASF AG was down 10 pfennigs at 65.80 marks.
